Two blockers remain in `26bbc75830204f6a80eb1359d6242ccb9dfbf295`, reviewing `b7e012d..HEAD`.

1. **P1 — Null stripping can turn accepted metadata into an unreadable inbox row.** EC-COORD-4/5.  
   The [environment check](/mnt/workspace/users/viperjuice/tmp/pl-panel-tlilcdob/review/reviewed-tree/supabase/migrations/20260930000000_coordination_server_time.sql:425) accepts `body: {"env":{"PATH":"/bin","unset":null}}`: its values are not exclusively strings. Persistence then applies [recursive `jsonb_strip_nulls`](/mnt/workspace/users/viperjuice/tmp/pl-panel-tlilcdob/review/reviewed-tree/supabase/migrations/20260930000000_coordination_server_time.sql:482), producing `{"env":{"PATH":"/bin"}}`. Executing the extracted frozen scanner confirmed no leaks before this transformation and `environment_dump` afterward. The [SDK validates the entire page](/mnt/workspace/users/viperjuice/tmp/pl-panel-tlilcdob/review/reviewed-tree/packages/state-ledger/src/supabase-coordination-channel.ts:73), so this row causes `malformed-response`, hiding valid messages. Preserve nested body nulls when omitting absent envelope fields, and validate the exact retained shape before effects.

2. **P1 — Environment-dump matching misses JavaScript line boundaries.** EC-COORD-4/5.  
   The [SQL pattern](/mnt/workspace/users/viperjuice/tmp/pl-panel-tlilcdob/review/reviewed-tree/supabase/migrations/20260930000000_coordination_server_time.sql:384) recognizes the string start and LF, whereas the frozen JavaScript expression uses multiline matching. For `body: {"note":"ordinary note\rPATH=/bin"}`, SQL’s checks admit the string, but the extracted frozen scanner reports `environment_dump`. U+2028 and U+2029 produce the same mismatch. This creates another successful-send/failed-page path. Match the frozen line-boundary semantics and add admitted SQL rejection cases asserting unchanged full inbox digests, including future timestamps.

The shared 48-rejection/13-acceptance corpus, timestamp controls, depth controls, and complete-page schema validation are useful additions, but neither counterexample is covered. SQL admission conclusions above follow source inspection; I executed extracted JavaScript scanner probes, not PostgreSQL or the full schema suite.

The earlier acquisition-clock, input-detachment, and arbitration repairs remain intact in the inspected boundaries. Frozen core contracts, RPC signatures, and privileges are unchanged. I reapprove the narrow `classify-limit.test.ts` redaction-only ownership amendment.

Verification: the worktree remained clean; `git diff --check` passed; all three repair bindings and the approved plan digest matched. Historical bindings matched their declared sources. Recorded hosted verification, admitted SQL, rehearsal, and producer-audit success bind `b7e012d`, before this SQL delta. Dependencies were absent; no installations, builds, or edits were performed.

All seven fresh reviews, current/final-HEAD verification and admitted SQL, source-bound rehearsal with publication skipped, observed producer audit, and postmerge CI remain required. R4 Opus remains `UNAVAILABLE`; historical local SQL remains failed. Pending gates are not additional code defects.

**SQL Metadata Traversal (supabase/migrations/20260930000000_coordination_server_time.sql)**
The `coordination_send_message` SQL function now enforces the complete JSON metadata policy via a breadth-first traversal array queue placed correctly before `pg_advisory_xact_lock` acquisition, pruning, and payload normalization.

Independent COORD R5 SQL metadata reconciliation review

Exact candidate: 26bbc75830204f6a80eb1359d6242ccb9dfbf295, clean immutable /home/viperjuice/workspace/coord-reviews/production-clone-round5. Review base: b7e012d2bb13504b4a14386aba0c343d5b4923c8. I executed the required current-head CR prescript before review, read its seven open issues/eight continuing items, the full R4 receipt, reconciliation, approved plan/criteria, complete delta and adjacent retained-message contracts. Qualified earlier findings carry only for unchanged source. This is a separate independent review, not a harness seat.

Three blocking findings

1. [P2] PostgreSQL whitespace matching still admits secrets rejected by the frozen reader (EC-COORD-4/5; metadata safety and valid-response contract).

supabase/migrations/20260930000000_coordination_server_time.sql:382 substitutes PostgreSQL \s/\S for JavaScript's character classes. In the actual PostgreSQL17 probe, a synthetic Bearer token separated by U+FEFF or U+00A0 was accepted. Extracted exact-source JavaScript scanning rejects both as bearer_token under packages/core-contracts/src/redaction.ts:23 and125. They have no other matching guard that compensates for the difference, so the SQL function can persist a body string that coordinationMessageSchema rejects. SDK list validation still parses the whole page at packages/state-ledger/src/supabase-coordination-channel.ts:73 and returns malformed-response at36-37. The former poisoned-page failure therefore remains.

Repair the inspection character classes to match the frozen ECMAScript whitespace set throughout the relevant patterns, without changing the stored strings or narrowing ordinary safe input. Add these Unicode cases, unchanged-state rejection and a following readable valid-page control to the admitted SQL test. Do not treat the existing shared corpus as exhaustive language equivalence proof.

2. [P2] JSONB decoding is not equivalent to JSON.parse for encoded metadata (EC-COORD-4/5; recursive metadata policy and preserved valid inputs).

At migration388-390 the validator attempts metadata_text::jsonb and treats invalid_text_representation as ordinary non-JSON text. PostgreSQL accepted the encoded body string {"password":"synthetic-value","note":"\ud800"}: its JSONB decoder failure was swallowed, so the sensitive password field was never recursively scanned. JavaScript JSON.parse accepts this syntax, and the exact frozen scanner rejects its decoded password field at redaction.ts127-128 and145. The SQL-admitted row can again invalidate the SDK inbox page. Conversely, safe encoded {"note":"\u0000"} has zero frozen-scanner leaks but SQL rejects it with 22P05. Safe encoded unpaired-surrogate text also has zero scanner leaks and was accepted. The decoder differences cannot be classified uniformly as invalid metadata or invalid JSON.

Make encoded-text inspection cover the JavaScript-valid decoded tree and preserve safe encoded values. Catching all PostgreSQL decode errors and ignoring them leaves the bypass; rejecting every such string narrows the frozen contract. Add positive null/surrogate controls and the password-plus-surrogate rejection control, asserting no retained-state mutation on refusal and a readable following valid page. No core schema relaxation is needed.

3. [P2] Publication changes the metadata after its validation (EC-COORD-4/5; exact retained-message conformance).

The traversal at migration374-442 checks the original body, but publication at482 applies recursive jsonb_strip_nulls(payload). For body {"env":{"PATH":"/bin","note":null}}, both the frozen scanner at redaction.ts146-147 and the SQL environment rule at425-426 accept the mixed-value object. Publication then deletes note:null, leaving env:{PATH:"/bin"}, which the frozen scanner rejects as environment_dump. The PostgreSQL probe confirms that the send succeeds and the null is not retained. My exact-source scanner probe independently confirms zero leaks before this transformation and environment_dump afterward. Consequently a valid accepted input still becomes a poisoned stored row.

Preserve nested body nulls while omitting absent optional envelope fields, or validate the exact representation that will be retained before locking/mutation. Any final-representation strategy must also preserve the frozen allowed-input behavior. Add the mixed environment/null input to the admitted positive controls and parse the complete retained page with the actual public schema. Validating only the pre-transformation input is insufficient.

Verified repairs and scope

The original plain password-body case is now rejected by the recursive key guard at migration430-433, before the advisory lock at443 and before normalization/pruning. The new traversal covers ordinary nested objects/arrays, encoded JSON, provider shapes, depth64 and numeric reader overflow; the written SQL regression uses the unchanged shared48 rejected/13 allowed corpus and adds timestamp/depth/numeric controls, exact retained-row digests and actual coordinationMessageSchema page parsing. I inspected those tests; I did not execute the suite or infer passing gates from their presence.

The placeholder exception at420-424 preserves the existing schema/value/reason/updatedAt shape and timestamp rules, and its values remain recursively inspected. fencingToken and boolean autoRefreshToken exemptions remain at430. No new RPC, function signature, privilege or public core contract is introduced. RLS/grants and lock order remain unchanged. The previous local clock, detached SDK/local messages and pre-backend arbiter validation repairs remain intact. I found no other delta regression. I reapprove the narrow classify-limit.test.ts ownership amendment at plans/phase-plan-v2-COORD.md:111: redaction test maintenance only, no classifier implementation or public-contract expansion. Continuing issues are not scope waivers.

Evidence boundary

I ran only read-only source/diff checks and extracted, in-memory exact-source metadata probes; no install, build, full tests, source mutation, private input, credentials or outward action. The shared external receipt /home/viperjuice/workspace/coord-reviews/sql-edge-probe-26bbc75.json binds this exact HEAD and migration digest ead0e60dcf8c9ffa1c546f48ea17af0cb272bb5721676d5d1587e764cfa89148. I read and checked that receipt; the parent executed its owned disposable internal PostgreSQL17 probes. Those observations are narrow evidence, not a local full SQL gate or a SQL suite I ran.

All three repair bindings match both their declared source 1fbdbf7b0ba42652c07d79c85136df4fd3e8e065 and current files. All84 COORD.json bindings match its historical measured source b7e012d; all84 archived a3e89d0 verification bindings also match their own source. The approved plan digest matches and Git whitespace checks pass. Historical failures/dissent remain preserved.
